papers.h: People born more recently enter old age with sharper memory that fades more slowly
papers.i: For decades, the chance of developing dementia at any given age has been dropping, but it has not been clear why.
papers.o: Later-born generations have better memory and lose it more slowly

papers.h: Lupus autoantibodies come from constantly renewed short-lived cells, mouse study finds
papers.i: Lupus is an autoimmune disease in which the immune system makes antibodies against the body's own molecules, such as DNA.
papers.o: Autoantibody origins in lupus and upon recurrence post CAR-T therapy

papers.h: A cleaner way to build peptides, in the same direction as cells
papers.i: Peptide drugs (short chains of amino acids) are in high demand, but the standard chemical way of making them is wasteful.
papers.o: Continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis

papers.h: HPV vaccination in Britain sharply cut high-risk HPV infections, but not equally
papers.i: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common sexually transmitted virus, and two types, HPV-16 and HPV-18, cause most cervical cancers.
papers.o: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, vaccination, and cervical screening in Britain from 1999 to 2024: findings from the repeated cross-sectional National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal)

papers.h: TB bacteria build cords by sharing one continuous membrane
papers.i: Mycobacteria, including the species that causes tuberculosis, have long been known to grow into twisted, rope-like bundles called cords, a feature linked to their ability to cause disease.
papers.o: A shared interbacterial membrane underlies mycobacterial cording

papers.h: Two electron qubits floating on solid neon made to work together
papers.i: Quantum computers are built from qubits, units of information that can hold combinations of 0 and 1 at once.
papers.o: Coherent manipulation of interacting electron qubits on solid neon

papers.h: Inside vaccinia virus: transcription machines paired up and an mRNA exit gate
papers.i: Poxviruses like vaccinia carry their own transcription equipment packed inside a protein-walled compartment called the core, so that as soon as the core enters a cell it can start making early messenger RNAs.
papers.o: Architecture of the poxvirus early-transcription machinery and portal complex

papers.h: Tiny heart-cell packages in blood offer a window into the living heart
papers.i: Studying what genes are active inside human heart muscle usually requires a tissue sample, which means an invasive biopsy. This study asked whether a simple blood draw could do the job instead.
papers.o: Cardiomyocyte-derived circulating extracellular vesicles enable a non-invasive liquid biopsy of human myocardium

papers.h: Changing how tungsten is spread inside fuel capsules improves fusion yields
papers.i: At the National Ignition Facility (NIF), powerful lasers heat a tiny gold container, which produces x-rays that crush a small fuel capsule until the fuel inside fuses.
papers.o: Improved Fusion Yields at the National Ignition Facility via Ramped-Profile Capsule Doping

papers.h: Excitons trapped in a lattice form several kinds of supersolid
papers.i: A supersolid is an unusual state of matter that combines two seemingly opposite properties: its particles sit in a regular, crystal-like pattern, yet they can also flow without friction, like a superfluid.
papers.o: Supersolid crystals of dipolar excitons in a lattice

papers.h: A modular way to build benzene rings carrying six different groups
papers.i: Benzene rings show up in more drug molecules than any other ring, yet benzenes with something attached at all six corners are almost never found in compound collections.
papers.o: Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations

papers.h: Testing four AI systems on real research-level maths problems
papers.i: Can today's AI systems correctly solve the kind of mathematics problems that working researchers actually run into?
papers.o: Harness design matters for AI capabilities in mathematics

papers.h: Pairing ruthenium and chromium atoms keeps an acid-water-splitting catalyst from dissolving
papers.i: Splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen in acidic electrolysers needs a catalyst for the oxygen-producing half of the reaction, known as the oxygen evolution reaction.
papers.o: Proximal single atoms for stable electrocatalysts

papers.h: Archaea use a newly found oscillating protein trio to find their middle before dividing
papers.i: Dividing cells must build their division machinery (the divisome) in the right place, usually the middle.
papers.o: A conserved oscillatory system that positions the divisome in Archaea

papers.h: TB bacterium's fatty sugar molecule can trigger coughing
papers.i: Tuberculosis spreads when people cough, but it has been unclear whether the bacterium itself makes chemicals that deliberately provoke the cough reflex.
papers.o: Mycobacterial phenolic glycolipid triggers ATP-mediated neuronal signalling and cough

papers.h: Hippocampus neurons blend each word's meaning with the words before it
papers.i: The meaning of a word shifts depending on the words around it.
papers.o: Linguistic contextualization in the human hippocampus

papers.h: Rituximab no better than azathioprine for keeping a rare vasculitis in remission
papers.i: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a rare disease in which small blood vessels become inflamed, usually alongside asthma and high levels of eosinophils, a type of white blood cell.
papers.o: Rituximab vs Azathioprine for Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis Maintenance

papers.h: Nasal flu vaccine for regular seasons protected ferrets from deadly cow-linked H5N1
papers.i: H5N1 bird flu has spread into dairy cattle, and a version of the virus taken from an infected person has raised concern about a possible human outbreak.
papers.o: Protective effect of seasonal vaccines against human-derived bovine H5N1 influenza virus

papers.h: Narrowing climate model forecasts for when northern lands lose their snow
papers.i: Climate models disagree about how quickly snow cover in the Northern Hemisphere will shrink as the planet warms.
papers.o: Observationally-constrained CMIP6 projections of a snow-free Northern Hemisphere

papers.h: Building plastic-like chains one unit at a time with light-driven chemistry
papers.i: Many everyday plastics are made by free-radical polymerization, where small building blocks called vinyl monomers link up in a fast chain reaction.
papers.o: Molar-mass- and sequence-defined vinyl macromolecules via iterative photoredox decarboxylative addition of α-substituted acrylates

papers.h: When can one experiment reveal the equations behind a system?
papers.i: Scientists often want to work out the equations governing a system, such as a set of differential equations, from measured data.
papers.o: A zero-one law for one-shot system identification

papers.h: Treating AI chatbot teams like computer networks predicts when teamwork helps
papers.i: Large language models (LLMs), the AI systems behind chatbots, have limits on how well a single model can reason, remember and perform.
papers.o: Language model teams as distributed systems

papers.h: Pulsar timing arrays may not reveal whether gravitational-wave background is Gaussian
papers.i: Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) watch many fast-spinning neutron stars whose radio pulses arrive like clockwork.
papers.o: Are Pulsar Timing Array Measurements Sensitive to Gravitational Wave Non-Gaussianities?

papers.h: Rearrangeable defect lines in liquid crystals could store information
papers.i: Liquid crystals, the materials used in many displays, are made of rod-like molecules that tend to point in the same direction. Where that common direction breaks down, lines called topological defects form.
papers.o: Encoding information into an embroidery of topological defects in liquid crystals

papers.h: Keeping two laser beams aligned lets 3D printing reach nanoscale detail deep inside material
papers.i: Tiny optical parts such as miniature lenses and on-chip light routers are often made by direct laser writing, a form of 3D printing where a focused laser hardens a light-sensitive material point by point.
papers.o: Depth-robust super-resolution nanofabrication for 3D mesoscopic photonic structures

papers.h: A single statistical toolkit finds cell-type-specific spatial signals across many tissue-mapping data types
papers.i: Spatial omics methods measure molecules (RNA, RNA variants, or open DNA regions) at thousands to millions of locations within a tissue slice.
papers.o: A unified framework for scalable differential testing for spatial omics

papers.h: Heart enzyme SMYD1 tags myosin to keep heart-cell contraction in check
papers.i: Heart muscle cells contract thanks to myosin, a motor protein that pulls on other filaments to shorten the cell.
papers.o: SMYD1 trimethylates myosin K129 to restrain cardiomyocyte hypercontractility

papers.h: More bird species mean more shared warnings about predators
papers.i: Ecologists know that having many species in an ecosystem tends to help it work well, but this idea has rarely been applied to animal behaviour.
papers.o: Species diversity increases information flow about predation in bird communities

papers.h: Dolphins with steadier, bigger social lives tend to live longer
papers.i: Earlier work across many animals has shown that average sociability tends to fall with age, often differently for males and females. But averages can hide how individuals differ.
papers.o: Distinct trajectories and predictability of individual grouping patterns in dolphins link social ageing to longevity

papers.h: Cash rewards helped more underserved smokers quit around lung cancer screening
papers.i: US health insurers require hospitals to offer help quitting smoking to people who come in for lung cancer screening, but it is unclear what kind of help works best for medically underserved groups.
papers.o: Smoking Cessation Among Underserved Patients Referred for Lung Cancer Screening

papers.h: AI reading routine heart tracings flags patients likely to have a treatable amyloid heart disease
papers.i: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is a condition in which a misfolded blood protein builds up in the heart muscle and causes heart failure.
papers.o: Electrocardiogram-Based Deep Learning to Prioritize Testing for Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy

papers.h: Four national surveys trace how sexual behaviour in Britain has changed since 1990
papers.i: How have the sexual lives of people in Britain changed over roughly three decades? This paper draws on Natsal, a set of large national surveys about sexual attitudes and lifestyles repeated at intervals from 1990 to 2024.
papers.o: Prevalence and trends in sexual behaviour in Britain from 1990 to 2024: findings from the repeated cross-sectional National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal)

papers.h: People who break rules for moral reasons are less deterred by punishment
papers.i: Legal systems in Western countries generally assume that punishment works by making crime costly, so a rational person will avoid it. In practice, though, punishment often does little to lower crime or reoffending.
papers.o: Morally motivated crimes are less sensitive to punishment

papers.h: How randomly built geometric functions spread their size and zeros evenly
papers.i: This pure-mathematics preprint (not yet peer reviewed) looks at random "holomorphic sections", which you can think of as smooth complex-valued functions living on a curved space (a compact complex manifold) and built from a line…
papers.o: Mass equidistribution and fluctuations for random holomorphic sections of big line bundles with continuous metrics

papers.h: Algae's own sticky chemicals help float blooms out of water without pumped air
papers.i: When algae bloom in lakes and reservoirs, they release algal organic matter (AOM), a mix of dissolved compounds usually treated as a pollutant.
papers.o: Carbon-neutral algal bloom management via algal organic matter repurposing

papers.h: Papers that open 'holes' between ideas pay off slowly but strongly
papers.i: New science often comes from combining existing ideas, but some combinations turn out far more fruitful than others.
papers.o: Knowledge gaps and scientific progress

papers.h: A fabric brightener helps pesticides form nanoparticles, and structure predicts which will
papers.i: Nanopesticides are pesticides packaged as tiny particles, billionths of a metre across, which can make them work better than conventional sprays.
papers.o: Quantitative prediction model of FB-113-driven self-assembly nanopesticides

papers.h: Paper wasps have brain cells tuned to their nestmates' faces
papers.i: Some paper wasps (the species Polistes fuscatus) can tell each other apart by the distinctive markings on their faces, much as people recognise one another by facial features.
papers.o: Neural correlates of facial recognition in a social wasp

papers.h: Brains of speakers of 21 languages appear to share a common meaning signal
papers.i: Do people who speak very different languages represent the meaning of what they hear or read in a similar way in the brain?
papers.o: A shared meaning component across languages in the human brain

papers.h: Bumpy 'egg-box' surface helps solid-state batteries discharge faster without failing
papers.i: Solid-state batteries replace the liquid inside a normal battery with a solid ceramic, and pairing that solid with a lithium metal electrode could store much more energy.
papers.o: Contouring mitigates voiding at the lithium/ceramic electrolyte interface on discharging solid-state batteries

papers.h: Researchers build a 'pangenome' map covering many mouse strains, not just one
papers.i: Lab mouse genetics has long relied on a single reference genome taken from one standard strain, called C57BL/6J. Comparing DNA from other mouse strains against this one sequence can miss or distort their differences.
papers.o: A draft mouse pangenome graph reference

papers.h: Brain growth charts built for Chinese populations differ from Western-based charts
papers.i: Doctors use growth charts to judge whether a child's height or weight is typical for their age.
papers.o: Towards population-specific brain charts across the lifespan

papers.h: Adding mRNA 'helper' proteins boosts DNA delivery into cells
papers.i: Getting therapeutic DNA to work inside cells is hard: the DNA has to cross from the cell's cytoplasm into the nucleus, where genes are read, and cells also have defences that chew up or silence foreign DNA.
papers.o: Modular mRNA-encoded helper proteins enhance DNA delivery

papers.h: Rearranging the same DNA switch parts decides where genes turn on
papers.i: Enhancers are short stretches of DNA that act like switches, telling a gene when and in which tissues to turn on. They work by providing landing spots (binding sites) for proteins called transcription factors.
papers.o: Exhaustive rearrangement of an enhancer reveals that dependency-syntax encodes tissue specificity

papers.h: Comparing how well different ocean chemistry tricks pull CO2 from the air
papers.i: Some proposed climate fixes aim to make the ocean absorb more carbon dioxide by changing its chemistry. One idea, ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE), adds alkaline substances to seawater.
papers.o: Global intercomparison of ocean-based geochemical carbon dioxide removal efficiencies

papers.h: Reweighting error-check data makes quantum error correction tolerate more noise
papers.i: Quantum computers protect information by spreading one 'logical' qubit across many physical qubits and repeatedly checking for errors. The pattern of check results is called the syndrome.
papers.o: Syndrome Resampling Enhances Quantum Error Correction Thresholds

papers.h: Twisted terahertz light passes its twist to a superconductor's Higgs mode
papers.i: Light can carry orbital angular momentum, a kind of twist in which the wavefronts spiral around the beam's axis like a corkscrew. A beam shaped this way is called a vortex beam.
papers.o: Imprinting Macroscopic Orbital Angular Momentum onto the Superconducting Higgs Mode Using a Terahertz Vortex Beam

papers.h: Proof that the 'rotation' reply always gives the second player an edge in a permutation game
papers.i: Penney's game for permutations works like this: two players each pick a different ordering pattern of length k (for example, 'small, large, medium' when k=3).
papers.o: The Rotation Strategy Wins Penney's game for Permutations

papers.h: AI safety tests disagree on what counts as a harmful chatbot answer
papers.i: Red teaming means deliberately trying to trick a large language model (LLM), the kind of AI behind chatbots, into producing harmful output.
papers.o: What Counts as Attack Success? Evaluating Harmfulness in Red Teaming LLMs

papers.h: Prime editing lets scientists tag thousands of proteins at once
papers.i: Biologists often want to attach a fluorescent or other tag to a protein in its natural place in the genome, so they can watch where it goes inside a cell. Doing this one gene at a time is slow.
papers.o: A prime-editing-based strategy for pooled protein tagging and subcellular localization mapping

papers.h: Mouse frontal cortex contains neurons that respond to very specific visual spots
papers.i: Vision in the mammalian brain is usually linked to the visual cortex at the back of the head, but the frontal cortex, a region more associated with planning and decision-making, also gets visual information.
papers.o: Highly selective visual circuits in mouse frontal cortex

papers.h: Leaves drift toward simpler shapes because simple shapes are easier to build
papers.i: Flowering plants have leaves ranging from simple, single blades to complex, divided forms such as compound or deeply lobed leaves.
papers.o: Developmental bias explains the evolutionary trend towards simple leaf shapes

papers.h: Million-person genetic study finds 27 new DNA regions linked to endometriosis
papers.i: Endometriosis, where tissue resembling the uterine lining grows outside the uterus, causes pain and fertility problems for roughly one in ten people with a uterus, yet its genetic causes are only partly understood.
papers.o: Multiancestry genome-wide association and integrative multiomics analyses implicate key pathways in endometriosis

papers.h: Ice-age Atlantic currents helped refill the North Pacific with oxygen
papers.i: Large patches of the ocean below the surface, called oxygen minimum zones, hold very little dissolved oxygen and today span more than 30 million square kilometres.
papers.o: Last glacial North Pacific oxygenation due to North Atlantic circulation changes

papers.h: A sum-of-series set whose fuzzy edge takes up most of its length
papers.i: Take an infinite list of positive numbers whose total is finite, and collect every number you can get by adding up some selection of them. The resulting set is called an achievement set.
papers.o: Measure-class classification of achievable Cantorvals

papers.h: Smarter memory shortcuts make long-text AI models generate faster
papers.i: When a large language model writes text one word at a time, it repeatedly looks back over a stored record of everything it has already processed, called the key-value (KV) cache.
papers.o: RefineKV: Query-Adaptive KV Cache Compression via Attention-Error Bounds

papers.h: A ready-made layered perovskite helps build steadier perovskite solar cells
papers.i: Perovskite solar cells are a fast-improving type of solar cell built from crystals with a particular structure called a perovskite.
papers.o: Promoted phase transition in perovskite heterojunctions via in-situ regulated 2D intermediates enables stable solar cells

papers.h: Strain-sensitive materials may give stronger magnet–electric links in thin films
papers.i: Some composite materials join two kinds of ingredients: a ferroelectric, which carries a built-in electric polarization (a separation of positive and negative charge), and a ferromagnet, like an ordinary magnet.
papers.o: Giant Room-Temperature Magnetoelectric Coupling Effect in Nanocomposite Thin Films via Strain-Sensitive Polarization

papers.h: A 3D-printed soft robot runs fast using air-powered circuits instead of electronics
papers.i: Soft robots are built from flexible materials and can be driven by fluid pressure, such as compressed air, rather than motors and chips.
papers.o: Printing powerful soft robots on a desktop

papers.h: Mapping where DNA copying stalls, one molecule at a time
papers.i: When a cell copies its DNA, a molecular machine called the replisome moves along the chromosome. If it hits an obstacle it can pause, and such pauses may lead to damage or rearrangements in the genome.
papers.o: Single-molecule landscape of DNA replication pausing

papers.h: A lipid-flipping enzyme pair keeps sound-sensing hair cells alive in mice
papers.i: Hair cells in the inner ear turn sound vibrations into electrical signals using tiny channels in their hair-like projections, called stereocilia.
papers.o: ATP8B1–TMEM30B flippase activity maintains stereocilia lipid asymmetry required for hearing

papers.h: Bacteria in tumours trigger TLR2, stripping away immune-suppressing Tregs
papers.i: Tumours often protect themselves by recruiting regulatory T cells (Tregs), which switch off killer immune cells.
papers.o: Bacteria-induced TLR2 signaling unleashes multiple mechanisms to reduce Treg immunosuppression and enhance cancer immunity

papers.h: Yeast mutant screens reveal how fungi resist 20 different antifungal drugs
papers.i: Fungal infections that shrug off several drugs at once endanger both human health and crops, so researchers need new antifungal compounds and a clear picture of how fungi become resistant.
papers.o: SATAY-based chemogenomic screening uncovers antifungal resistance mechanisms and key determinants of ATI-2307 and chitosan sensitivity

papers.h: Switching off a liver enzyme could treat rare metabolic diseases
papers.i: Lysine, an amino acid from food, is broken down in a chain of chemical steps.
papers.o: Oligonucleotide-mediated AASS silencing as a potential therapeutic strategy for ALDH7A1 deficiency and glutaric aciduria type I

papers.h: Soybean plants use a cell wall ingredient to keep nodule bacteria in check
papers.i: Soybeans and other legumes host helpful bacteria called rhizobia inside small root swellings called nodules, where the bacteria turn nitrogen from the air into a form the plant can use.
papers.o: Host control of rhizobial proliferation in soybean nodules

papers.h: Engineered light-powered enzyme steers a tricky ring-forming reaction
papers.i: Electrocyclizations are reactions where an open chain of molecules curls up and closes into a ring. They can be triggered by heat or light, and the direction the ends twist as they join decides which mirror-image product you get.
papers.o: An artificial photoenzyme constrains substrates for selective antarafacial electrocyclizations

papers.h: Farming intensification in Sumatra changes which species live where, not just how many
papers.i: Demand for farm products worldwide has grown over recent decades, pushing more intensive land use into some of the planet's most species-rich tropical regions.
papers.o: Tropical land-use intensification reshapes biodiversity in expected and unexpected ways

papers.h: El Niño years made famines more likely and longer in Europe, 1500–1800
papers.i: El Niño is the warm phase of a Pacific Ocean climate cycle that shifts weather patterns around the world from one year to the next.
papers.o: El Niño amplified food insecurity in early modern Europe from 1500 to 1800

papers.h: Faulty RNA editing in blood rises with age and partly runs in families
papers.i: Before a gene's message (RNA) is used to build a protein, non-coding stretches called introns are normally cut out and the remaining pieces joined in different combinations, a process called alternative splicing.
papers.o: Longitudinal changes in mis-splicing in a cohort of female twins are widespread and highlight mechanisms of ageing

papers.h: People born later reach old age with sharper memories that fade more slowly
papers.i: Over the past few decades, the chance of developing dementia at a given age has dropped in Europe and the United States.
papers.o: Generational gains in cognitive capacity and dementia incidence rates in Western countries

papers.h: In richer countries, food's toll on wildlife stops rising with wealth
papers.i: As countries get richer, people usually eat more and buy different foods, which can mean more farmland and more harm to wild species.
papers.o: Biodiversity footprints of food consumption decouple from economic growth at high income levels

papers.h: Chemists finally bottle oxoboranes, long-sought molecules with a boron–oxygen triple bond
papers.i: Oxoboranes are molecules in which a boron atom is bonded to only two neighbouring atoms, one of them an oxygen held by a triple bond.
papers.o: Isolable crystalline oxoboranes

papers.h: Inherited ALK mutation stalls nerve-cell development, setting stage for neuroblastoma
papers.i: Neuroblastoma is a childhood cancer that starts in cells of the sympathoadrenal lineage — nerve-and-adrenal-forming cells that develop from the embryonic neural crest.
papers.o: ALK R1275Q expands Schwann cell precursor-like cells during sympathoadrenal commitment, creating a permissive state for neuroblastoma initiation

papers.h: Self-correcting quantum memory outlasts the best uncorrected qubit in its own device
papers.i: Quantum bits lose their fragile information quickly, so quantum computers need error correction.
papers.o: Extending qubit lifetime beyond break-even and enhancing quantum sensing by autonomous quantum error correction

papers.h: Regular polygons have the highest 'free-edge' vibration tone for their size
papers.i: Imagine a flat polygon-shaped plate or drum whose edges are free to move rather than clamped. Its lowest nonzero natural vibration frequency is captured by a number called the first positive Neumann eigenvalue.
papers.o: The regular $N$-gon maximizes first positive Neumann eigenvalue among simple polygons with at most $N$ sides and fixed area

papers.h: Any three-letter choices at each position can build an endless square-free word
papers.i: A 'square' in a word is a block repeated twice in a row, like 'abab' or 'xyzxyz'. Mathematicians have long known that infinite words with no squares exist using just three letters.
papers.o: Avoiding squares over words with lists of size three

papers.h: Better-connected surface layer pushes perovskite solar cells near 28% efficiency
papers.i: Perovskite solar cells are a newer kind of solar cell that now nearly match the efficiency of standard silicon panels.
papers.o: Band-Edge-Extended Heterointerfaces for Perovskite Solar Cells and Tandems

papers.h: A 1.29-gram flapping-wing robot flies using only its own sensors and computer
papers.i: Tiny flying robots the size of insects usually cannot keep themselves stable on their own. Instead, they rely on external cameras (motion-capture systems) and off-board computers that track their position and send corrections.
papers.o: Controlled flight of an insect-scale flapping-wing robot via integrated onboard sensing and computation

papers.h: Controlling light's phase on chips by tuning losses instead of refractive index
papers.i: Programmable photonic circuits, chips that route and process light, usually steer light by changing the refractive index of a material (how much it slows light).
papers.o: Non Hermitian synthetic phase shifter with topologically protected phase control via tunable losses

papers.h: A helper protein lets microbes make a toxic cancer drug without poisoning themselves
papers.i: Many natural products made by microbes, such as antibiotics and anticancer compounds, depend on redox chemistry (reactions that move electrons around).
papers.o: Balancing redox-mediated cytotoxicity and catalysis in natural product biosynthesis

papers.h: Nickel catalysts steer reactions to build four kinds of alkene from similar ingredients
papers.i: Alkenes are molecules that contain a carbon–carbon double bond, and they appear throughout medicines, materials and other useful chemicals.
papers.o: Sorting reaction pathways to program alkene skeletons

papers.h: Reinforcement learning can repair AI math reasoning taught with flawed examples
papers.i: Large language models are often trained in two steps. First comes supervised fine-tuning (SFT), where the model copies worked example solutions.
papers.o: Reinforcement Learning Unlearns Corrupted SFT Reasoning

papers.h: AI interpretability test can be fooled by 'parasite features'
papers.i: Researchers who try to understand how neural networks work often use a framework called Causal Abstraction.
papers.o: Parasite Features: Causal Abstraction Through Spurious Pathways

papers.h: Two quasars sit inside an unexpectedly hot gas bubble in the early universe
papers.i: Quasars are galaxies whose central supermassive black holes are swallowing matter and shining extremely brightly.
papers.o: Excess intergalactic heating around a dual quasar system 2.8 Gyr after the Big Bang

papers.h: Machine learning helps design a 3D-printed titanium alloy that is both strong and stretchy
papers.i: Titanium alloys are prized for being light and strong, but making them much stronger usually makes them more brittle.
papers.o: Nanostructures strengthen titanium alloys

papers.h: Combining 2D and 1D materials to build complementary computer-chip circuits
papers.i: Modern computer chips rely on CMOS (complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor) logic, which pairs two kinds of transistors: n-type, which conduct using electrons, and p-type, which conduct using 'holes' (missing electrons).
papers.o: Mixed-dimensional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology for high-performance integrated circuits

papers.h: 3D X-ray movies show which hidden structures make battery electrode grains work harder
papers.i: Lithium-ion battery electrodes are packed with particles, pores and binder, and how this 3D structure controls performance is hard to see while a battery is actually running.
papers.o: Four-dimensional X-ray nano-holotomography reveals multiscale chemomechanics in composite graphite–silicon battery electrodes

papers.h: AI that reads scenes and signs helps a four-legged robot hike kilometres
papers.i: Robots with legs can now walk well over rough ground, but deciding where to go is still hard: a pile of rocks is easy to detect, while a puddle, a private pasture or a 'road work' sign is not.
papers.o: Bridging vision-language reasoning and learned control for legged navigation in the wild

papers.h: Lab-grown brain immune cells from 261 people link genes to dementia risk
papers.i: Microglia are the brain's resident immune cells, and many genetic variants linked to Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, multiple sclerosis and ALS seem to act in them.
papers.o: Integrated QTL mapping and CRISPR screening in pooled iPSC-derived microglia reveals genetic drivers of neurodegenerative risk

papers.h: Brain immune cells may help mice forget motor skills by eating myelin
papers.i: Learning a new movement skill involves the brain adding fresh myelin, the fatty insulating wrap around nerve fibres, made by cells called oligodendrocytes.
papers.o: Microglia mediate motor memory decay through activity-dependent phagocytosis of myelin sheaths

papers.h: Lungfish reuse a toxin to rebuild their skin for life on land
papers.i: When African lungfish face drying conditions, they enter estivation, a dormant state similar to hibernation, and their skin changes to form a protective cocoon.
papers.o: Evolutionary repurposing of a pore-forming toxin drives epithelial remodeling during terrestrial adaptation

papers.h: Bacteria detect virus-infected algae and help speed up bloom collapse
papers.i: Algal blooms are sudden, massive population booms of tiny ocean algae. They matter because the algae pull carbon dioxide out of the air and turn it into living material, which then feeds the rest of the marine food web.
papers.o: Bacteria and viruses team up to hasten the demise of algal blooms

papers.h: Defibrillators did not cut combined sudden death and dangerous arrhythmia in scarred, mildly weak hearts
papers.i: Current guidelines reserve preventive implantable defibrillators (ICDs, devices that detect and shock dangerous heart rhythms) for people whose heart pumps out 35% or less of its blood per beat.
papers.o: CMR to Guide Defibrillator Implantation for LVEF

papers.h: Fatty liver disease in lean people carries similar risks to obese cases
papers.i: Fatty liver disease linked to metabolic problems (now called MASLD) is usually thought of as a condition of people with obesity, but it also shows up in people of normal weight.
papers.o: Histologic Features and Clinical Outcomes of Lean Metabolic Dysfunction–Associated Steatotic Liver Disease

papers.h: Dual-target CAR T cells for hard-to-treat myeloma pass first safety test
papers.i: Multiple myeloma is a blood cancer of antibody-making plasma cells. One treatment, CAR T-cell therapy, reprograms a patient's own immune T cells to attack a protein on myeloma cells called BCMA.
papers.o: Natural ligand-based CAR T-cell therapy targeting BCMA and TACI for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (TriPRIL): a non-randomised, phase 1, first-in-human trial

papers.h: Silencing a liver enzyme protects mice from a toxic metabolic disease
papers.i: Glutaric aciduria type I (GA-1) is an inherited disease in which a missing enzyme, glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase, blocks one step in the breakdown of the amino acid lysine.
papers.o: Rescue of glutaric aciduria type I by GalNAc-conjugated siRNA against aminoadipate semialdehyde synthase

papers.h: Gentle brain stimulation at alpha rhythm boosts reward learning and eases low mood
papers.i: Learning from rewards relies on brain circuits linking the front of the brain to deeper structures. A key signal is the reward prediction error: the gap between the reward you expected and the reward you actually got.
papers.o: Temporal interference stimulation targeting the ventromedial prefrontal cortex enhances reward learning and improves depression scores

papers.h: Atlantic Gulf Stream changes can warm the North Pacific through the Arctic air
papers.i: In recent years, ocean surface temperatures have run unusually high across much of the Northern Hemisphere outside the tropics.
papers.o: Kuroshio Extension warming shaped by Gulf Stream variability via the Arctic atmosphere

papers.h: Pairing home energy upgrades with solar could help poorer households save more
papers.i: Moving homes away from fossil fuels relies on technologies such as rooftop solar panels and efficient appliances, but these tend to end up in wealthier homes.
papers.o: Targeted technology coadoption for reconciling energy savings and equity gains in the residential energy transition

papers.h: Damaged lysosomes form internal protein clumps that slow leakage of their contents
papers.i: Endolysosomes are small membrane-bound compartments inside cells that break down material taken in from outside.
papers.o: Endolysosomal damage promotes intraluminal protein condensate formation that limits cytosolic leakage

papers.h: An aging-related plant protein helps a heat-response protein survive in warm weather
papers.i: Plants change how they grow when temperatures rise, for example by stretching their stems, a response called thermomorphogenesis. A key controller of this response is a protein called PIF4.
papers.o: ORE1 stabilizes PIF4 protein through a UBP12/UBP13-dependent regulatory module in thermomorphogenesis

papers.h: Brain scans with millisecond timing show how we come to feel a limb is ours
papers.i: How does the brain produce the feeling that our arm belongs to us?
papers.o: Spatiotemporal brain dynamics of limb ownership perception

papers.h: How Baltic Sea plankton and weather shape gases swapped with the air
papers.i: Seawater both gives off and absorbs many small carbon-containing gases called volatile organic compounds (VOCs).
papers.o: Marine volatile organic compounds air-sea exchange dynamics across a summer-to-autumn ecosystem transition

papers.h: Words people use often are more likely to exist across many languages
papers.i: Some ideas, like CHILD or SUN, have their own dedicated word in nearly every language, while others, like PARENT or WEATHER, often do not.
papers.o: Usage frequency predicts lexicalization across languages

papers.h: Complete pig genomes reveal moving centromeres and genes behind high-altitude adaptation
papers.i: Most pig genetics relies on a single reference genome that still has gaps, especially in hard-to-read repetitive regions such as centromeres (the chromosome 'waist' that guides chromosome separation during cell division).
papers.o: High-quality pig pan-genome resources illuminate centromere evolution and enhance genotype–phenotype mapping

papers.h: Two new four-drug tuberculosis combinations pass an early screening trial
papers.i: Standard treatment for tuberculosis (TB) uses four drugs (isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, called HRZE) for 24 weeks.
papers.j: The New England Journal of Medicine
papers.o: Assessing Multiple Treatment Regimens for Tuberculosis

papers.h: Weekly semaglutide injections lowered BMI in children aged 6 to 11 with obesity
papers.i: Semaglutide, a once-a-week injected drug, is already approved to treat obesity in teenagers and adults, but there has been little evidence on whether it works in younger children.
papers.j: The New England Journal of Medicine
papers.o: Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity in Children 6 to <12 Years of Age

papers.h: Google quantum chip wins cooperation games beyond any classical strategy
papers.i: Can quantum effects let players coordinate better than any classical plan allows, even when they cannot talk to each other?
papers.o: Quantum-classical separation in bounded-resource tasks arising from measurement contextuality

papers.h: A calcium catalyst shuttles fluoride ions to build fluorine-containing molecules
papers.i: Many industrial catalysts rely on transition metals such as palladium, which work through well-understood steps where the metal grabs and releases molecular fragments.
papers.o: Calcium catalysed nucleophilic fluorination

papers.h: Astronomers weigh a distant black hole by watching gas swirl around it
papers.i: Giant black holes at the centres of galaxies pull on the gas and stars close to them.
papers.o: Resolving the black hole sphere of influence in a hyperluminous obscured quasar at redshift 4.6

papers.h: How a hormone and a pill-like drug switch on the same heart receptor differently
papers.i: RXFP1 is a receptor on cell surfaces that responds to relaxin, a natural hormone.
papers.o: Divergent activation of the RXFP1 relaxin receptor by protein and small-molecule agonists

papers.h: A clock-gene deletion helps heat-loving mosquitoes mate and carry more malaria
papers.i: Anopheles stephensi is a mosquito that spreads malaria and has recently spread into Africa, where it copes well with hot city conditions. The researchers wanted to know what genetic changes let it handle the heat.
papers.o: A natural mutation of timeless enhances mosquito thermal adaptation and malaria parasite transmission

papers.h: Glacial lakes explain only a small share of glacier loss worldwide
papers.i: When a glacier ends in a lake, the water can speed up melting and the breaking off of ice at the glacier's front.
papers.o: Climate and glacier geometry dominate global glacier–lake interactions

papers.h: Simulations show a 'lens' trick could make light states with exactly 10,000+ photons
papers.i: A Fock state is a state of light holding an exact, definite number of photons, unlike laser light, whose photon count fluctuates.
papers.o: Scalable Generation of Macroscopic Fock States Exceeding 10,000 Photons

papers.h: Tiny light-powered sensors wirelessly track heat inside running chemical reactions
papers.i: Chemists often want to watch a reaction as it happens, but doing so usually requires specialized instruments, specially built reaction vessels, or pulling samples out of the mixture, which can disturb it.
papers.o: Telemetric calorimetry for wireless continuous reaction profiling

papers.h: A lattice-math shortcut finds a hidden gamma-ray pulsar in hours, not centuries
papers.i: Pulsars are rapidly spinning, collapsed stars that send out beams of radiation, and some can be detected through regular pulses of gamma rays.
papers.o: Gamma-Ray Pulsar Discovery Using a Lattice-Based Method

papers.h: Better internal contacts let thick solid-state lithium–sulfur battery electrodes hold more charge
papers.i: Lithium–sulfur batteries could store much more energy for their weight than today's lithium-ion cells, and making them "all-solid-state" (using a solid material instead of a liquid to carry lithium ions) could make them safer.
papers.o: High-loading all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries enabled by tailored sulfur–sulfide and sulfur–carbon interfaces

papers.h: A soft, liquid-free rubber that carries ultrasound with little loss
papers.i: Ultrasound scans need a soft layer between the probe and the skin so sound waves pass through without being lost.
papers.o: Interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer for low-loss soft ultrasonic interfaces

papers.h: An AI 'virtual scientist' designs working RNA molecules from scratch
papers.i: RNA molecules can do jobs beyond carrying genetic messages: some cut other RNA (ribozymes), some grip small molecules and light up (aptamers).
papers.o: Programmable functional RNA design with a virtual scientist

papers.h: A tug-of-war over unfinished RNA tunes mitochondria and brain development
papers.i: Before a gene's message can be used to make protein, the cell copies it into a precursor RNA (pre-mRNA) and then cuts out non-coding stretches called introns, a step known as splicing.
papers.o: The fate of poised pre-mRNAs shapes mitochondrial activity and cellular differentiation

papers.h: Lab-grown immune brain cells link disease gene variants to cell behaviour
papers.i: Many DNA variants that raise the risk of neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's or Parkinson's are thought to act through microglia, the brain's resident immune cells.
papers.o: Tracing genetic risk of neurodegenerative disease through variants affecting microglial function

papers.h: 85,000 virus genomes show who actually spread COVID, and where
papers.i: Researchers wanted to know how much SARS-CoV-2 actually spread inside particular places — schools, colleges, nursing homes — compared with the background risk of catching it anywhere in the community.
papers.o: Genomic surveillance reveals age-structured SARS-CoV-2 transmission across settings

papers.h: Jumping-gene insertion cripples a key gene in a rare movement disorder
papers.i: X-linked dystonia-parkinsonism (XDP) is a rare inherited brain disease found mainly in men, linked to a chunk of 'jumping DNA' (an SVA retrotransposon, a repetitive sequence that copies itself around the genome) that landed…
papers.o: Genome writing reveals SVA retrotransposon consequences in X-linked dystonia-parkinsonism

papers.h: Vitamin B3 supplement failed to slow early Parkinson disease in large trial
papers.i: Nicotinamide riboside is a form of vitamin B3 that the body converts into NAD, a molecule cells need to produce energy.
papers.o: Nicotinamide Riboside for Patients With Early-Stage Parkinson Disease

papers.h: Magnetic reconnection may slow down as plasma systems get bigger
papers.i: Magnetic reconnection is the process in which magnetic field lines in a plasma (a hot gas of charged particles) break and re-join, suddenly releasing stored magnetic energy as particle motion; it powers solar flares and space…
papers.o: System Size Dependence of Collisionless Reconnection Rate

papers.h: Ring-shaped porphyrin molecules carry an electron current around the whole belt
papers.i: Chemists are interested in molecular 'belts': closed loops of linked rings whose electron clouds point outward, like the staves of a barrel.
papers.o: Globally antiaromatic anthracene–porphyrin nanobelts

papers.h: Part of the Milky Way's 'Norma arm' may actually be the bar's shock front
papers.i: Our galaxy is usually drawn with four main spiral arms and a central bar, an elongated structure made of stars whose size and speed are still argued over.
papers.o: The nature of the Norma arm as a bar-driven star-forming shock front

papers.h: New zeolite catalysts combine tiny and larger pores to crack heavy oil better
papers.i: Zeolites are crystalline minerals made of aluminium, silicon and oxygen, riddled with pores narrower than a nanometre.
papers.o: Meso–microporous zeolitic materials with thin walls containing ordered 10-ring channels

papers.h: Light-patterned soft layers stack into stretchy, breathable skin electronics
papers.i: Skin-like electronic devices often need several stacked layers of wiring, and those layers must be linked by tiny vertical connections called VIAs (vertical interconnect accesses) that pass through the insulating material between…
papers.o: Monolithic tiered microlithography for stretchable multilayer electronics with high-density, soft, and ultrathin VIAs

papers.h: RNA folding drives species-dependent host mRNA partitioning in Ebola virus condensates
papers.i: RNA viruses form membraneless condensates in host cells to drive replication, but whether these compartments regulate host RNAs remains unclear.
papers.o: RNA folding drives species-dependent host mRNA partitioning in Ebola virus condensates

papers.h: The low-pitch end of the inner ear does not follow the usual pitch map
papers.i: Textbook hearing theory says each spot along the coiled cochlea (the snail-shaped hearing organ of the inner ear) responds most strongly to one particular pitch, so that pitch is laid out along the coil like keys on a piano.
papers.o: Denoised vibrometry reveals noncanonical filtering at the apex of the cochlea

papers.h: A single block of genes turns would-be winged ant queens into wingless ones
papers.i: Ant colonies contain distinct body types, called castes, such as workers and queens, and some species have evolved entirely new castes. How these new forms arise genetically and during development has been unclear.
papers.o: A supergene converts queen-destined larvae into a novel caste in ants

papers.h: Pooled studies suggest exposing frogs to chytrid fungus can protect them
papers.i: Chytrid fungus (Bd, short for Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis) is a skin pathogen that has caused severe declines in amphibians around the world.
papers.o: Meta-analysis shows that immunization reduces amphibian susceptibility to the chytrid fungus

papers.h: A PEG substitute for mRNA nanoparticles shifts delivery away from the liver
papers.i: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are the fatty bubbles that carry mRNA into cells, as in COVID-19 vaccines. To keep them stable in the bloodstream they usually include polyethylene glycol (PEG), a water-loving polymer.
papers.o: PEG-free tunable poly(2-oxazoline) lipids modulate mRNA-LNP biodistribution and expression in vivo

papers.h: Psilocybin and ketamine make mice slower but more accurate decision-makers
papers.i: Drugs like psilocybin (the active compound in 'magic mushrooms') and ketamine are being studied as fast-acting treatments for mental health conditions, but it is unclear how they change the way the brain makes choices.
papers.o: Psychedelics shift decision strategies and reconfigure orbitofrontal dynamics

papers.h: Brain ripples in the hippocampus grow while people hold images in short-term memory
papers.i: The hippocampus, a seahorse-shaped structure deep in the brain, is best known for long-term memory.
papers.o: Ramping-up hippocampal ripples and their neocortical coupling support human visual short-term memory

papers.h: Satellites catch an Ethiopian volcano releasing record amounts of methane without erupting
papers.i: Volcanoes normally give off very little methane, yet magma pushing into carbon-rich sedimentary rock is thought to have released huge amounts of greenhouse gas during episodes of sudden climate change in Earth's past.
papers.o: Methane outburst driven by magma–sediment interactions at Fentale Volcano detected by satellite

papers.h: Pacific low-oxygen zone barely changed through the last three ice ages
papers.i: Off the Pacific coast of Central America lies an oxygen-deficient zone (ODZ), a mid-depth layer of seawater with almost no oxygen. In it, microbes strip usable nitrogen out of the ocean (denitrification).
papers.o: Insensitivity of the North Pacific oxygen-deficient zone to recent ice age cycle climate changes

papers.h: More realistic plankton in climate models predict a bigger drop in ocean carbon storage
papers.i: The ocean's 'biological pump' is the process by which tiny drifting organisms (plankton) take up carbon near the surface, and some of that carbon then sinks into the deep sea when they die or are eaten.
papers.o: Plankton ecological complexity amplifies climate-driven weakening of the ocean biological pump

papers.h: Cutting carbon helps health and nature but may not ease resource demands
papers.i: This study asks what happens to the environment and to raw materials when the world follows different routes to deep decarbonization, meaning large cuts in the greenhouse gases released by energy and industry.
papers.o: Environmental and material implications of global climate mitigation pathways

papers.h: Switching California homes from gas to electric pays off mainly where AC exists
papers.i: Replacing gas furnaces, water heaters and stoves with electric versions is central to climate plans, but California's electricity is expensive, so it is unclear whether households come out ahead.
papers.o: Exploring the distributional implications of targeted residential electrification in California

papers.h: Thin air on the Tibetan Plateau stops Varroa mites from breeding
papers.i: Varroa mites are tiny parasites that live on the outside of honey bees and are the most damaging pest beekeepers face, so most beekeepers must treat their hives with mite-killing chemicals again and again.
papers.o: Altitude-induced hypoxia suppresses Varroa mite reproduction in Tibetan honey bees

papers.h: Tuning where acid sits inside hot-running fuel cells improves their output
papers.i: High-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells use a polymer membrane soaked in phosphoric acid to carry protons (hydrogen ions) between electrodes.
papers.o: A membrane-guided strategy for optimizing proton exchange membrane fuel cells via spatially controlled acid distribution

papers.h: Light-activated carbon dots made from plants target a major wheat fungus
papers.i: Fungi that attack crops cause large financial losses and threaten the world's food supply. One of the worst is Fusarium head blight, a fungal disease that infects the grain-bearing heads of wheat.
papers.o: Plant-derived photocatalytic carbon dots for crop disease management

papers.h: Vaccinating whole communities against malaria each season cut infection rates
papers.i: Malaria in parts of West Africa spreads mostly during a rainy season, so researchers asked whether vaccinating entire communities just before that season could lower how many people carry the parasite.
papers.o: Seasonal mass vaccination with R21/Matrix-M against malaria in The Gambia and Burkina Faso: an open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial

papers.h: Newly found gut viruses are poxviruses' closest known relatives
papers.i: Large double-stranded DNA viruses are common in soil and water but have rarely been spotted inside animal digestive systems.
papers.o: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide

papers.h: Astronomers watch a star spiral inside its giant partner's outer layers
papers.i: Many tight pairs of stars, including the compact stellar remnants that orbit each other closely, are thought to start out much farther apart.
papers.o: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion

papers.h: Brain region that controls metabolism and sleep cycles shrinks in Alzheimer's
papers.i: The hypothalamus is a small region deep in the brain that helps run body functions such as metabolism, hormone release and daily (circadian) rhythms.
papers.o: Hypothalamic volume and cell-type changes in ageing and Alzheimer’s disease

papers.h: Tiny diamond particles help perovskite solar cells withstand heat and long use
papers.i: Halide perovskites are crystals that turn sunlight into electricity very efficiently, partly because their atomic lattice is soft and flexible.
papers.o: Elastic-field reorganization stabilizes soft-lattice perovskites for durable solar cells

papers.h: Farming intensity in Indonesia reshuffles which species live where, not just how many
papers.i: Most studies of biodiversity in tropical farmland count species at a single spot, missing how farming changes the mix of species across a whole landscape and across many kinds of organisms.
papers.o: Tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity

papers.h: Homo erectus lived in southern China's rainforests later than once thought
papers.i: Homo erectus, an early human species, existed for a very long time, from roughly 1.9 million years ago until about 108,000 years ago, and spread from Africa across to eastern Asia.
papers.o: Rainforest adaptation in late Homo erectus from southern China

papers.h: Bogong moths steer by the tilt of Earth's magnetic field, using light
papers.i: Bogong moths travel up to about 1,000 km twice a year between where they breed and a limited set of cool resting sites in the Australian Alps, where they spend summer in a dormant state.
papers.o: Bogong moths navigate with a light-dependent geomagnetic inclination compass

papers.h: Molecular recorder traces family tree of over a million mouse embryo cells
papers.i: How does a single fertilized egg give rise to all the cell types of a mammal? Watching this directly is hard because development happens deep inside tissues we cannot easily see into.
papers.o: A DNA Typewriter records the cell lineage history of a mouse, from zygote to late organogenesis

papers.h: A small patch of the brain's 'listening' area helps plan spoken words
papers.i: Wernicke's area, a region toward the back of the left temporal lobe (the side of the brain near the ear), has long been viewed as the hub for understanding speech.
papers.o: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke’s area

papers.h: Organic nitrogen falling from the air feeds the oceans more than thought
papers.i: Nitrogen is a key nutrient for ocean life, and some of it reaches the sea from the air.
papers.o: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans

papers.h: A molecular 'glue' layer helps large perovskite solar panels hold together
papers.i: Perovskite solar cells convert sunlight to electricity efficiently and cheaply, but they tend to degrade, partly because the layers inside them can weaken or come apart at their boundaries.
papers.o: Molecular adhesion for durable metal halide perovskite modules

papers.h: Twisted laser light makes a trapped ion spin in measurable steps
papers.i: Light can carry angular momentum, a measure of rotation, in two ways. One is spin, tied to the beam's polarization, and it is well known to govern which atomic transitions are allowed.
papers.o: Angular momentum transfer from an optical vortex to an atomic rotor

papers.h: Gut inflammation after a myeloma CAR T therapy often persists and can be fatal
papers.i: CAR T cell therapy reprograms a patient's own immune cells to attack cancer. One version targets BCMA, a protein found on the cancer cells of multiple myeloma, a blood cancer.
papers.o: Multicenter characterization of enterocolitis associated with BCMA-directed CAR T cell therapy

papers.h: Early-life stress primes a brain pathway that worsens pain in female mice
papers.i: Children who experience adversity are more likely to develop chronic pain and anxiety as adults, and this link appears stronger in women. This mouse study asked what brain wiring might carry that risk forward in time.
papers.o: A thalamo-amygdalar circuit drives female vulnerability to chronic pain after early-life stress

papers.h: Hollow shells with one opening use turbulence to sort and trap particles
papers.i: Turbulent flow looks random, but its swirls (eddies) pass energy from large scales down to small ones in an organised way that is not in thermal equilibrium.
papers.o: Quiet within, chaos without: Turbulence shelters drive selective particle capture and release
